body:
Similarly to #36123, the ui2 windows confuse `:$q`, which doesn't close the last window on the tab, but targets a hidden ui2 window.

The problem seems to be a combination of using
`FOR_ALL_WINDOWS_IN_TAB()`, which includes all windows (hidden, non-focusable, etc), and then counting the windows without factoring in `win_has_winnr()`.

There are examples of using `win_has_winnr()`, such as:
- [`eval/buffer.c`'s `buf_win_common()`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/4a5062cda69fa6cb59b7dc0c488dfb05accf99de/src/nvim/eval/buffer.c#L474-L475)
- [`eval/window.c`'s `f_getwininfo()`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/4a5062cda69fa6cb59b7dc0c488dfb05accf99de/src/nvim/eval/window.c#L130-L135)
- [`window.c`'s `win_get_tabwin()`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/4a5062cda69fa6cb59b7dc0c488dfb05accf99de/src/nvim/window.c#L7860-L7869)

But possibly problematic ones:
- `ex_docmd.c`'s:
	- [`invalid_range()`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/4a5062cda69fa6cb59b7dc0c488dfb05accf99de/src/nvim/ex_docmd.c#L3891-L3893)
		- ^ should this include hidden windows? Can a user address them by number? `win_has_winnr()` suggests not
	- [`ex_close()`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/4a5062cda69fa6cb59b7dc0c488dfb05accf99de/src/nvim/ex_docmd.c#L5233-L5244)
	- [`ex_hide()`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/4a5062cda69fa6cb59b7dc0c488dfb05accf99de/src/nvim/ex_docmd.c#L5478-L5484)
- `eval/window.c`'s:
	- [`f_winrestcmd()`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/4a5062cda69fa6cb59b7dc0c488dfb05accf99de/src/nvim/eval/window.c#L797-L808)
	- [`find_win_by_nr()`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/4a5062cda69fa6cb59b7dc0c488dfb05accf99de/src/nvim/eval/window.c#L172-L180)


See also #36123

comment_data.body:
This should never be the case - we should always have a winnr since we should always be called on the current window, or `win == NULL` (so we never get here):

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/4a5062cda69fa6cb59b7dc0c488dfb05accf99de/src/nvim/ex_docmd.c#L1177-L1178

Too defensive?

This feels a bit hacky. Perhaps we should have a flag against commands whose address type is `ADDR_WINDOWS` for whether they operate on numbered windows, or all windows?

Or we split `ADDR_WINDOWS` to itself and `ADDR_NUMBERED_WINDOWS` ?

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/4a5062cda69fa6cb59b7dc0c488dfb05accf99de/src/nvim/ex_cmds.lua#L2209-L2214
Please don't make random changes to oldtests.

comment_data.body: what is a non-nr window? does that mean windows in other tabpages?

It's a window that doesn't have a number, so those that are either hidden or not focusable:

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/fbcb7a056cef7a5efd7aa7f494365a04b1c86895/src/nvim/eval/window.c#L44-L49

Perhaps I should rename this argument, any preference?
`include_hidden_nonfocusable`
`include_special`

> Perhaps we should have a flag against commands whose address type is `ADDR_WINDOWS` for whether they operate on numbered windows, or all windows?

worth exploring in a separate pr

comment_regular_data.body: I've kept the change isolated to fixing `:$q`, but I'm happy to fix/refactor the remaining incorrect (if deemed incorrect) uses of window-counting. i.e. uses of `FOR_ALL_WINDOWS_IN_TAB()` that don't guard a `winnr++` with `win_has_winnr()`

The test failures are to-do with focusable windows:

<details><summary>Test failures</summary>

```
FAILED   ...vim/build/Xtest_xdg_ui/test/functional/ui/float_spec.lua @ 490: float window supports windo with focusable and non-focusable floats

```

</details>

In short, I expect `:windo` is `break`ing early here:

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/4a5062cda69fa6cb59b7dc0c488dfb05accf99de/src/nvim/ex_cmds2.c#L676-L686

because `eap->line2` is now the focusable window count. This is because the test tests focusable windows:

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/4a5062cda69fa6cb59b7dc0c488dfb05accf99de/test/functional/ui/float_spec.lua#L495-L498

and `win_has_winnr()` says that focusable windows don't have a window number:

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/4a5062cda69fa6cb59b7dc0c488dfb05accf99de/src/nvim/eval/window.c#L44-L48

So I think we need to have `:windo`'s default range include non-focusable windows, but `:q`'s default range (i.e. the range for when `$` is given) exclude them.

> kept the change isolated to fixing `:$q`, but I'm happy to fix/refactor the remaining incorrect (if deemed incorrect) uses of window-counting

would be much appreciated 👍 

ideally, the decision should be owned by one centralized function
Window counting factored into a single function (`win_find_nr`) and other comments addressed. Will see what CI says...

[Static analysis failure](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/actions/runs/30396486574/job/90400573298?pr=40992) looks bogus, seems to assume that `curtab` can be null:

> src/nvim/eval/window.c|54 col 5| note: Null pointer value stored to 'tp'

(and then passed to a nonnull parameter)

well, we need the ci to pass... you can just add `assert(curtab)` or sth like that

Thanks for the merge, meant to say, looks like the test that's failing (`test/functional/terminal/channel_spec.lua`) is doing so in other PRs, [for example here](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/41097), with some history of it being flaky - #37968. I can submit a timeout bump if that'd help?
For some tests, I think we need a more convenient "retry" util: https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/35764
